description: Evaluation cases for the Kajola skill. Each case defines a prompt, required sections, and specific assertions that must hold in the generated output.

cases.name: Artisan booking marketplace (Nigeria)
cases.prompt: Design a multi-tenant artisan booking platform for Nigeria called Kajola. Artisans (barbers, tailors, mechanics) create profiles and get booked. Clients discover and pay via Paystack. Need full system architecture.

assertions.description: Phone OTP is the primary auth method
assertions.check: output contains 'phone' and 'OTP' in Section 1 or Section 2

assertions.description: Paystack is specified as payment provider
assertions.check: output contains 'Paystack' in Section 2, Section 3, and Section 8

assertions.description: SQL schema has RLS on all tables
assertions.check: every CREATE TABLE block in Section 3 has a corresponding ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY statement

assertions.description: Booking conflict prevention at DB level
assertions.check: output contains 'EXCLUDE USING gist' or 'prevent_booking_conflict' trigger in Section 3

assertions.description: Offline queue included in mobile structure
assertions.check: output contains 'offline' or 'offline-queue' in Section 5

assertions.description: All env vars named and sourced
assertions.check: Section 8 contains a table with NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, PAYSTACK_SECRET_KEY, TERMII_API_KEY
output contains 'HMAC' or 'webhook signature' in Section 7 or Section 4
Section 9 contains percentage values (e.g. '5%', '2.5%') and Naira amounts (e.g. '₦' or 'NGN')
Section 10 contains '10,000' or '10k' and '100,000' or '100k' and '1,000,000' or '1M'
output contains '## Assumptions Made'
Section 1 mentions at least two distinct user roles (e.g. artisan/provider and client)

cases.name: Equipment rental marketplace (East Africa)
cases.prompt: Build the complete system design for ToolHire Pro — an equipment rental marketplace for East African construction companies. Multi-tenant. M-Pesa payments. Full package.

assertions.description: M-Pesa is included as primary payment method
assertions.check: output contains 'M-Pesa' or 'Daraja' in Section 2, Section 3, and Section 4
output contains 'KES' or 'Kenya shilling' or 'multi-currency'
Section 3 contains a conflict prevention mechanism for rental slot overlaps
output contains 'tenant_id' and 'current_user_tenant_id' in Section 3
Section 3 contains tables for equipment/inventory, rentals, and availability
Section 3 or Section 4 addresses security deposit or damage tracking
Assumptions block mentions East Africa or Kenya as target market

cases.name: Food delivery platform (Ghana)
cases.prompt: Design a food delivery platform for Accra, Ghana. Restaurants list menus, customers order, riders deliver. Need multi-restaurant support, real-time order tracking, and Flutterwave payments in GHS.

assertions.check: output contains 'Flutterwave' in Sections 2, 4, and 8
output contains 'GHS' or 'Ghana cedi' or 'pesewa'
output contains 'Realtime' or 'WebSocket' or 'real-time' in Section 2 or Section 5

assertions.description: Three roles present: customer, restaurant, rider
assertions.check: Section 1 mentions three distinct personas or roles

assertions.description: Menu and order tables in schema
assertions.check: Section 3 contains tables for menus (or menu_items) and orders (or order_items)
Section 3 or Section 2 addresses rider location updates (PostGIS or coordinates)
Section 7 includes events for order state transitions (placed, accepted, picked_up, delivered)

cases.name: Minimal prompt — defaults applied correctly
cases.prompt: Design a home cleaning services marketplace.

assertions.description: All 11 sections present despite minimal prompt
assertions.check: output contains all 11 section headers
output contains 'Paystack' or 'Termii' or 'phone OTP'
output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions stack defaults

assertions.description: No placeholder text despite sparse input

assertions.check: Section 3 contains tables relevant to cleaning services (bookings, service_types, cleaners, or similar)

cases.name: Custom stack override respected
cases.prompt: Build a freelance marketplace for African creatives (designers, writers, developers). Use Stripe for payments and Firebase for auth instead of Supabase. Target market: pan-African.

assertions.check: output contains 'Stripe' in Sections 2, 4, and 8

assertions.description: Firebase auth used instead of Supabase Auth
assertions.check: output contains 'Firebase' in Sections 2 and 5
output mentions multiple African countries or currencies in Section 9 or Section 10
Section 3 contains tables for gigs/projects, proposals/bids, and contracts or milestones
Assumptions block mentions Firebase and Stripe as user-specified overrides

cases.name: Quality gate — zero placeholders enforcement
cases.prompt: Design a telemedicine platform for Nigeria. Doctors consult patients via video. Prescriptions managed digitally.

assertions.description: No placeholder text anywhere in output

assertions.check: output names a specific video provider (Daily.co, Twilio Video, Agora, Whereby, or similar)
Section 3 contains a prescriptions table with at minimum: id, patient_id, doctor_id, medications, issued_at
output mentions data privacy compliance (NDPR for Nigeria or equivalent) in Section 1 or Section 8
Section 3 contains booking conflict prevention for doctor appointments

assertions.description: All API endpoints have error cases
assertions.check: every endpoint block in Section 4 contains at least one 'Errors:' entry
Section 9 contains at least one specific Naira amount (₦) or percentage with a digit

cases.name: Ride-hailing dispatch with M-Pesa and USSD (Kenya)
cases.prompt: Design a boda-boda (motorcycle taxi) dispatch platform for Nairobi, Kenya. Riders join Saccos, passengers book and pay via M-Pesa STK Push, fares are settled via M-Pesa B2C payout. Feature-phone riders need a USSD fallback for earnings checks. Full system architecture.

assertions.description: M-Pesa STK Push used for passenger payments
assertions.check: output contains 'STK Push' or 'STK' or 'Daraja' in Sections 3, 4, or 8

assertions.description: M-Pesa B2C used for rider payouts
assertions.check: output contains 'B2C' or 'BusinessPayment' or 'payout' in Sections 3 or 4
output contains 'KES' or 'Kenya shilling' in Sections 2, 3, or 9
output contains 'USSD' in Sections 3, 4, or 5

assertions.description: Rider and passenger as distinct personas
assertions.check: Section 1 contains at least two distinct personas (rider and passenger)
Section 3 contains geography or PostGIS or ST_DWithin for rider location

assertions.description: Africa's Talking or Termii for SMS fallback
assertions.check: output contains 'Africa\'s Talking' or 'Termii' in Sections 3 or 8
Section 3 contains tenant_id and RLS policies
output contains 'offline' or 'queue' or 'cache' in Sections 5 or 6
Section 4 or Section 8 contains HMAC or signature verification for M-Pesa callbacks

assertions.description: Assumptions block present with Kenya-specific notes
assertions.check: output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions Daraja or Safaricom or CBK

cases.name: Bilingual and offline-first compliance (West Africa)
cases.prompt: Design a micro-logistics platform for Accra, Ghana and Abidjan, Côte d'Ivoire. Small parcels booked by phone, delivered by independent couriers. Bilingual UI (English + French). Orange Money payments for Côte d'Ivoire, MTN Mobile Money for Ghana. Couriers often lose connectivity during deliveries.

assertions.description: Orange Money or MTN Mobile Money referenced
assertions.check: output contains 'Orange Money' or 'MTN Mobile Money' or 'MTN MoMo' in Sections 3 or 4

assertions.description: Multi-currency: GHS and XOF both addressed
assertions.check: output contains 'GHS' and ('XOF' or 'CFA' or 'franc')
output contains 'French' or 'fr-' or 'bilingual' or 'i18n' in Sections 1, 5, or 8
output contains 'offline' or 'SQLite' or 'queue' or 'sync' in Sections 5, 6, or 9
Section 3 contains parcel or shipment status states (e.g. picked_up, in_transit, delivered)

assertions.description: Sender and courier as distinct personas
assertions.check: Section 1 contains at least two personas: one who sends parcels and one who delivers
Section 3 contains 'ROW LEVEL SECURITY' and 'tenant_id'
Section 5 specifies phone OTP as the authentication method
output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire or Abidjan

cases.name: Multi-staff beauty salon with SORF lifecycle and loyalty (Kenya)
cases.prompt: Design a multi-tenant beauty salon booking platform for Nairobi, Kenya called GlamPlus. Customers book appointments with specific stylists, pay a 30% M-Pesa deposit to confirm, earn loyalty points, and join a waitlist if their preferred stylist is fully booked. Salon owners manage multiple branches and see real-time KPI dashboards. Full system architecture.

assertions.check: Section 3 contains booking_status enum with at least: pending, confirmed, held, checked_in, in_progress, completed, cancelled, no_show, disputed
Section 3 contains 'availability_windows' with day_of_week and start_time and end_time

assertions.description: Booking conflict exclusion constraint scoped to staff and branch
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'EXCLUDE USING gist' with staff_id and branch_id

assertions.description: Deposit policy as jsonb on businesses table
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'deposit_policy' in businesses or tenants table as jsonb
Section 3 or Section 7 contains 'waitlist' and a trigger or automation event for cancellation
Section 3 contains 'loyalty_accounts' or 'loyalty_transactions' or 'loyalty_points'

assertions.description: M-Pesa STK Push used for deposit collection
assertions.check: Section 3 or Section 4 contains 'STK Push' or 'Daraja' or 'M-Pesa' for deposit payment

assertions.description: Branch KPI dashboard or materialised view present
assertions.check: Section 3 or Section 7 contains 'branch_kpis' or 'kpi' or 'materialised view' or 'materialized view'
Section 3 contains 'no_show' as a booking state and Section 7 or Section 3 references no-show policy or penalty
Section 3 contains 'held_until' or 'hold' and a pg_cron or automation job to release expired holds

assertions.description: Assumptions block mentions Kenya and M-Pesa
assertions.check: output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions Kenya or KES and M-Pesa or Daraja

cases.name: Multi-branch health clinic with franchise management and SORF (Nigeria)
cases.prompt: Design a multi-branch health clinic appointment platform for Nigeria called MedBook. Patients book appointments at any HealthFirst clinic branch, pay a ₦5,000 deposit via Paystack to confirm, and receive SMS reminders. Doctors manage their own availability. The clinic group owner sees cross-branch analytics. Full system architecture.

assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'businesses' and 'branches' and 'staff' tables reflecting the multi-branch structure

assertions.description: SORF booking states including checked_in and in_progress
assertions.check: Section 3 contains booking_status with 'checked_in' and 'in_progress' as distinct states
Section 3 contains 'availability_windows' for doctor/staff scheduling
Section 3 or Section 4 contains 'Paystack' and 'idempotency' or 'idempotency_key' for deposit flow

assertions.description: Franchise owner cross-branch view or materialised view
assertions.check: Section 3 or Section 5 contains 'franchise' or 'cross-branch' or 'branch_kpis' or 'aggregate' dashboard
Section 3 or Section 7 contains 'no_show' handling with policy enforcement (deposit forfeiture or prepayment requirement)

assertions.description: All API endpoints have auth requirements documented
assertions.check: Section 4 documents auth requirement for every endpoint (Bearer JWT or none for public endpoints)
Section 7 contains a cron job or automation event for appointment reminders (24h or 2h before)
Section 9 contains at least one specific Naira amount (₦) for deposit, subscription, or commission

cases.name: Home services marketplace with SORF job lifecycle (Nigeria)
cases.prompt: Design a multi-tenant home services marketplace for Nigeria called FixIt. Customers book verified plumbers, electricians, and AC technicians. The provider arrives, assesses the job, collects a ₦3,000 call-out deposit via Paystack, does the work, and the customer pays the balance on completion. Providers set their own weekly availability. Customer no-shows trigger a prepayment requirement. Full system architecture.

assertions.description: SORF booking states including checked_in and in_progress
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'checked_in' and 'in_progress' as distinct booking states
Section 3 contains 'availability_windows' with day_of_week and start_time

assertions.description: EXCLUDE USING gist constraint for slot conflict prevention
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'EXCLUDE USING gist' for booking conflict prevention
Section 3 or Section 4 contains 'Paystack' for deposit payment flow

assertions.description: NGN amounts in Section 9 (no placeholder rates)
assertions.check: Section 9 contains at least one specific Naira amount (₦) for fees, subscriptions, or commissions
Section 3 or Section 7 contains no_show_policy or 'require_prepayment' or 'prepayment'

assertions.description: Deposit policy stored as jsonb on businesses
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'deposit_policy' as jsonb on businesses or tenants table

assertions.description: Customer and provider as distinct personas
assertions.check: Section 1 contains at least two personas: one who books and one who provides the service
Section 7 or Section 4 contains 'HMAC' or 'x-paystack-signature' for webhook verification
Section 3 or Section 4 or Section 7 contains 'idempotency' or 'idempotency_key'
output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions Nigeria or NGN or Paystack

cases.name: Multi-branch healthcare clinic with USSD fallback (East Africa)
cases.prompt: Design a multi-branch hospital appointment platform called MediCare Connect for East Africa (Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania). Patients book doctor appointments, pay a KES 500 / UGX 20,000 / TZS 10,000 consultation deposit via M-Pesa (Kenya), MTN Mobile Money (Uganda), or M-Pesa Tanzania. Rural patients with feature phones use USSD to check appointment status. Doctors manage their own schedules. Hospital group owners see cross-branch analytics. Full system architecture.

assertions.check: output contains 'KES' and ('UGX' or 'Uganda') and ('TZS' or 'Tanzania')

assertions.description: M-Pesa used for Kenya and Tanzania; MTN MoMo for Uganda
assertions.check: output contains 'M-Pesa' and ('MTN' or 'Mobile Money') in Sections 2, 3, or 8

assertions.description: USSD fallback for rural feature-phone patients
assertions.check: output contains 'USSD' in Sections 3, 4, or 5

assertions.description: Africa's Talking used for SMS or USSD delivery
assertions.check: output contains 'Africa\'s Talking' or 'africastalking' in Sections 2 or 8

assertions.description: SORF booking states in schema including checked_in
assertions.check: Section 3 contains 'checked_in' as a booking status
Section 3 contains 'availability_windows' for doctor or staff scheduling
Section 3 or Section 5 contains 'branch_kpis' or 'cross-branch' or 'franchise' or 'aggregate' analytics
Section 3 contains 'ROW LEVEL SECURITY' and 'tenant_id'
Section 3 or Section 7 contains 'no_show' handling
Section 3 or Section 4 or Section 7 contains 'idempotency_key' or 'idempotent'
output contains '## Assumptions Made' and mentions Kenya and ('Uganda' or 'Tanzania')

scoring.notes: A case passes if 85% or more of its assertions pass. The skill passes overall if all 12 cases pass. Target: 12 cases, 113 assertions.
